title: On-call audit runbook: RBAC v2 evidence & SIEM export
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a pragmatic on-call runbook for preparing, packaging, and answering auditor questions related to RBAC v2, audit log schema, evidence automation, and SIEM export. Focus is SOC 2 (CC6, CC7) and ISO 27001 (A.9, A.12) mapping. Use this doc during live auditor sessions or for pre-engagement evidence bundles.

Quick summary (one-liner):
- How to produce a 48-hour evidence bundle showing role modifications, policy changes, and corresponding audit log exports plus SIEM ingestion proofs; checklist for auditor Q&A.

Owner and escalation: 
- Primary: Maya Chen (security-and-compliance)
- Backup: Alejandro Ruiz (platform-security)
- Escalation path: security manager -> Head of Trust -> CTO (use Slack #sec-oncall then pager)

What auditors will ask (common and nasty):
- Show where roles and permissions are stored, proof of change history, and who approved changes.
- Demonstrate that audit logs capture both API and console actions, including failed attempts and admin overrides.
- Prove logs are immutable (or append-only) and exported to SIEM with integrity checks.
- Evidence of retention policy and automated backups for the retention window tied to SOC 2/ISO requirements.
- Show how automated evidence snapshots are produced and who has access to those snapshots.

Mapping to controls (short):
- SOC 2: CC6 (logical access), CC7 (system operations) -> RBAC role definitions, role assignment logs, periodic access reviews, audit log exports, SIEM correlation rules.
- ISO 27001: A.9 (access control) -> role matrix exports, proof of least-privilege enforcement; A.12 (operations security) -> logging, monitoring, log retention and integrity.

Evidence sources (where to collect from):
- RBAC v2 metadata: git repo infra/rbac-v2/roles.yaml and PR history (GH PRs) for role model changes.
- DynamoDB/Aurora tables: role_assignments table (read replica snapshot).
- Audit log store: logs-audit-prod (JSONL daily shards) with schema fields listed below.
- SIEM export: Splunk/hec index name: redwood-audit, export manifest: exports/redwood-audit-YYYYMMDD.json.gz.
- Evidence automation: runbook job logs in CI job: pipelines/evidence-snapshot (run id, artifacts).
- Access review docs: monthly review Confluence page and access-review CSV attachments.

Audit log schema (canonical fields we commit to provide):
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- event_id (uuid v4)
- request_id (parent correlation id)
- actor_id (user id / service principal)
- actor_type (human | service | system)
- actor_role_list (roles at time-of-event, comma-separated)
- action (string, CRUD style + domain e.g., role.create, token.issue)
- resource_type (e.g., project, model, deployment, org)
- resource_id (string)
- outcome (success | failure | denied)
- client_ip (IP or CIDR)
- user_agent (if available)
- session_id (if session-based)
- prev_state_hash (sha256 of resource state pre-change)

Notes on schema:
- prev_state_hash + event_id allow auditors to verify the before/after accounted for. We publish the hash algorithm and salt in the evidence README.
- All events are JSONL, newline-delimited, compressed. We retain raw and canonicalized copies for 730 days by default.

How to produce a 48-hour evidence bundle (step-by-step):
1) Toggle to evidence staging project: export credentials from vault path: secret/evidence/export-readonly.
2) RBAC snapshot: 
   - git archive --prefix=rbac-snap/ HEAD:infra/rbac-v2 > rbac-snap.tar
   - Query role_assignments table: SELECT * FROM role_assignments WHERE updated_at >= (now()-48h) ; write CSV to evidence/role-assignments-48h.csv
   - Export PRs: gh pr list --search "repo:infra/rbac-v2 updated:>={date}" --json number,title,author > rbac-prs.json
3) Audit logs: 
   - Use logs export job: aws s3 cp s3://logs-audit-prod/2025-01-15/ redwood-evidence/tmp/ --recursive --exclude "*" --include "audit-2025-01-1?.jsonl.gz"
   - Run the canonicalizer: tools/audit-canon --input redwood-evidence/tmp --out canon/ --schema-version v3
4) SIEM proof: 
   - Export Splunk search job: index=redwood-audit earliest=-48h latest=now() | outputcsv splunk-audit-48h.csv
   - Export export-manifest.json.gz from exports/ and include the pipeline job id and HEC checksum.
5) Integrity pack: 
   - Create sha256sum of all files and sign with internal key: gpg --detach-sign --armor sha256sums.txt
6) Bundle: tar czf audit-bundle-YYYYMMDD-48h.tgz canon/ splunk-audit-48h.csv rbac-snap.tar role-assignments-48h.csv rbac-prs.json sha256sums.txt sha256sums.txt.asc
7) Upload to evidence S3: aws s3 cp audit-bundle-*.tgz s3://redwood-evidence/rbac-v2/2025/ --acl private

Checklist for on-call prior to auditor session:
- [ ] Confirm the evidence S3 path and read ACL for auditor temporary user.
- [ ] Confirm retention policy on the specific artifacts (matches SOC 2 attestation window).
- [ ] Verify the prev_state_hash algorithm doc is included in the bundle.
- [ ] Prepare short demo script showing role change -> audit log -> SIEM alert (use test-org/test-project).

Common auditor questions and suggested answers (scriptable):
Q: Where are role definitions authored and reviewed?
A: Authoring happens in infra/rbac-v2 repo. Changes are reviewed via GitHub PRs (link included in bundle). Each PR must include a documented rationale and a reviewer from security or platform. Our mandatory PR checklist includes testing role scoping and impact analysis.

Q: How do you prove a role assignment was performed by an authorized approver?
A: We provide role_assignments rows with created_by and approval_request_id fields. Approval artifacts are stored in the approvals service (approval:APP-####) and a snapshot of the approval thread is included. We also provide the PR and the audit event that contains event.action=role.assign and outcome=success.

Q: How do you ensure logs weren't tampered with?
A: Logs are written to append-only S3 with object lock enabled for the root prefix. We publish sha256sums and GPG-signed manifests. Splunk ingestion verifies checksums on receipt. In the bundle we include original S3 object metadata (etag) and ingestion job ids.

Q: What about service/service-account activity?
A: actor_type indicates service vs human; for service actors we include the deployment id and the service owner. We also include a brief mapping doc service_accounts_map.csv.

Known gaps and mitigations (short & current):
- gap-1: historical role assignment deltas prior to 2023-06 lack prev_state_hash. mitigation: explain retention start date and provide manual diffs from git history for older changes. ticket: JIRA:SEC-312 (owner: Priya)
- gap-2: a handful of low-volume control-plane actions previously wrote to legacy-logs index. mitigation: we backfilled legacy exports and validated event_id continuity. ticket: JIRA:SEC-389 (owner: Evan)
- gap-3: automated evidence runbook does not yet include SIEM proof-of-ingest checksum. mitigation: roadmap item in backlog -> pipelines/SEC-evidence-HEC-check (ETA: Q2).

Remediation owners & timeline (short):
- Priya Nambiar: backfill prev_state_hash for pre-2023 records (2025-03-01 target)
- Evan Brooks: complete legacy index backfill validation (2025-02-15 target)
- Alejandro Ruiz: add HEC checksum step to evidence pipeline (2025-04-01 target)

Evidence sampling policy for auditors:
- Provide contiguous 48-hour window around the requested timeframe by default. For controls requiring quarterly evidence provide one 7-day contiguous sample per quarter. For change events we provide +/- 24-hour context for each event_id.

Operational notes (on-call tips):
- If an event seems missing, first check canonicalizer logs (tools/audit-canon.log) for parse errors. Common cause: non-UTF8 payloads from legacy agents. Fix: re-run canonicalizer with --fallback-encoding latin1.
- For time drift issues, convert all timestamps to UTC and include the offset file tz-offsets.csv from the bundle.
- If auditors request elevated access to S3, create a time-bound IAM role and document session tokens in the audit record (record STS session id).

Retention and legal notes: 
- Default retention: 2 years for raw audit logs, 5 years for signed manifests and access-review artifacts (policy owner: Legal/Compliance).
- If an auditor requests longer retention for a specific engagement, escalate to Legal for a retention change request.

Appendix: quick links and commands (copy/paste)
- Canonicalize: ./tools/audit-canon --input s3://logs-audit-prod/2025-01-15/ --out /tmp/canon --schema v3
- Splunk export example: splunk search "index=redwood-audit earliest=-48h" --outputcsv splunk-audit-48h.csv
- Evidence upload: aws s3 cp audit-bundle-*.tgz s3://redwood-evidence/rbac-v2/2025/ --profile evidence-uploader

Open questions (work-in-progress):
- Do we want to embed signed JSON-LD manifests describing RBAC role lineage? (discuss in next architecture review)
- Should we include a notarization service for larger enterprise audits? (legal intake required)

If you're running this with an auditor in the room: follow the checklist, produce the bundle, and use the "demo script" section to show the end-to-end flow. Keep the conversation focused on mapping artifacts -> control requirement, and avoid getting pulled into operational detail unless asked.

Last updated notes:
- 2025-01-17: added prev_state_hash explanation + new canonicalizer v3 fields.
- 2024-11-06: initial draft.

End of runbook.
